_doc: Headwaters source registry - Bengaluru episodic sources. Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local). CADENCE + TIER ARE DOCUMENTATION ONLY - decided 2026-07-26. Neither gates polling: every non-ciBlocked entry is fetched on every weekly run whatever its declared cadence (48 HTTP requests per CI run across ~26 hosts). Deliberate. (1) Cadence is a CLAIM and claims are wrong - CPCB is 'yearly' and shipped a mid-year Yamuna-only file, BBMB was recorded frozen and had resumed, CHIRPS looked daily and publishes monthly; gating polls on a declared cadence inherits every such error and stops looking at exactly the source that surprised you. (2) A conditional check is a check that can silently stop - the WRIS 'green for 39 days while ingesting nothing' bug lives in skip logic. (3) Interval scheduling is maintenance overhead for no real saving at this volume. Cadence earns its place at REVIEW time instead: it tells you whether a detection is plausible - a 'yearly' source producing a new edition three weeks after the last is itself a signal.

sources.notes: The single highest-value unwatched Bengaluru source before 2026-07-26. It is the ONLY longitudinal price/dependency series for the tanker market and it carries the entire /bangalore/tanker page plus 2 facts. Survey rounds are irregular (2015, 2019, 2024, a 2025 round reported via opencity.in/bengaluru-water-tankers-survey-2025-situation-better-than-2024) so a scheduled watch is the only way to catch the next one. Verified 2026-07-26: 3 resources, metadata_modified 2025-11-27. Schemas differ by round - not every field exists for every year and n= counts differ - so a new round is a SCHEMA-BREAK candidate, not a routine roll-forward. NOTE the dataset slug: facts-bangalore.json used to cite opencity.in/data/bengaluru-tanker-water-survey, which 404s; the live path is data.opencity.in/dataset/bengaluru-tanker-water-data (fixed 2026-07-26). NVDM Bangalore migration 2026-07-30: licence corrected TWICE: first to CC BY-NC per the CKAN API generic id, then (review 2026-07-30) to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 per the resource pages' explicit statement - NON-COMMERCIAL and SHARE-ALIKE encumbered; dependsOn widened to tanker-context (2025-round rate-gap context) and supply-overview (tanker_market block).

sources.refreshMethod: manual PDF parse + digitization of the critically-over-extracted ward list
sources.notes: IISc Groundwater Outlook for Bengaluru (April 2025) - the 80 critically-over-extracted wards that are the city's HEADLINE groundwater layer (rendered directly on /bangalore, not behind /groundwater). Watched via the OpenCity mirror deliberately: IISc's own host wgbis.ces.iisc.ac.in returns 403 to curl even with a browser UA (verified 2026-07-26) and cannot be watched. Verified: 1 resource, metadata_modified 2025-11-27. A new Interim Report or Outlook edition would land as a new resource. Caveat: the mirror lags the publisher, so a detection here is a floor, not a ceiling. LICENCE: OpenCity CKAN package_show returns license_id 'cc-nc' / license_title 'Creative Commons Non-Commercial (Any)' / license_url creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/2.0 (verified 2026-07-31). The registry previously recorded this as 'open (per OpenCity dataset page)', which was wrong: this source carries the Bengaluru groundwater layer rendered on /bangalore (the critically-over-extracted wards), so the non-commercial term reaches the city's headline groundwater surface.

sources.refreshMethod: manual (WRIS GEC extract; IN-GRES payload capture still open)
sources.notes: Karnataka side of the same assessment watched for TN by ingres-gw-assessment-tn - deliberately a separate entry because the dependsOn differ and a GEC round can land per state. Backs the all-6-blocks-Over-Exploited headline, Bangalore-East at 306% draft/recharge and Yelahanka 140% -> 260% over 2020-2024. Same caveat as the TN entry: http-meta watches the IN-GRES SPA build (Last-Modified + ETag verified 2026-07-26), not the assessment data, so expect false positives on redeploy and replace once the payload capture lands. LICENCE: verified by fetching ingres.iith.ac.in and grepping the full Angular app bundle (main.*.js, 2.0 MB): zero occurrences of a copyright policy, terms of use, disclaimer or licence statement - the only 'Policy' matches are Leaflet's referrerPolicy option and the only 'terms' match is an FAQ sentence about years of data (verified 2026-07-31). CGWB is the fallback authority.

JICA Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Project Phase 3 Final Report (Nov 2017) is the anchor document behind bangalore-supply-overview.json, which cites 13 sources in total. Watched via the OpenCity mirror because BWSSB's own site is not watchable: bwssb.karnataka.gov.in/info-1/About+BWSSB/en carries no document links at all, only accessibility boilerplate (verified 2026-07-26), and there is no tenders/notifications page with stable hrefs. Verified: 6 resources, metadata_modified 2025-11-27. KNOWN GAP: BWSSB's live announcements (Stage V/VI progress, tariff, connection numbers) are therefore still unwatched - they enter the platform through dated press citations. Also note the host: www.bwssb.karnataka.gov.in does NOT resolve over HTTP; use bwssb.karnataka.gov.in without the www (fixed across citations 2026-07-26). LICENCE: OpenCity CKAN package_show returns license_id 'other-pd' / license_title 'Other (Public Domain)' with no license_url and no grant text (verified 2026-07-31). The site-wide OpenCity terms (opencity.in/terms-and-conditions) say 'Data are licensed under: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and ODbL' and permit download 'for non-commercial and / or personal use only', which conflicts with the per-dataset label; the publisher never issued a public-domain dedication.
